statutoryAuthority.ruleStatement: An individual convicted of a misdemeanor, or of a series of misdemeanors arising from a single incident, may petition the court in which the conviction occurred to restrict access to the criminal history record information. The court shall grant the order if the individual has completed the terms of the sentence, has not been convicted of any crime in any jurisdiction excluding nonserious traffic offenses for at least four years immediately preceding the filing, has no pending charged offenses, and the harm to the individual clearly outweighs the public's interest in the information being publicly available. Section 35-3-37(w) applies the paragraph to sentences imposed before, on or after July 1, 2020. The four-year period runs backward from the filing date, any intervening conviction resets it, and sentence completion is a separate and additional requirement. A lifetime maximum of two convictions may be restricted under § 35-3-37(j)(4), a petition denied on the same conviction may not be refiled within two years of the final order, and the § 35-3-37(j)(4)(B) list excludes specified family-violence, sexual, theft and serious traffic offenses. Restriction limits who may see criminal history record information and sealing under subsection (m) closes the clerk's file; neither destroys the record, and neither gives the individual a right to deny that a restricted arrest or conviction exists.
doNotImport: Do not quote a filing fee or a pauper's-affidavit rule; whether a Georgia clerk charges a fee for a filing in an existing criminal case, and whether O.C.G.A. § 9-15-2 reaches it, are recorded as unresolved and county-specific.
Do not treat the four-year conviction-free period as a period that must pass after sentence completion; it runs backward from the filing date.

Do not decide whether the offense sits on the § 35-3-37(j)(4)(B) exclusion list, whether an out-of-state conviction inside the four-year window breaks the clock, or whether both lifetime slots have been used; each is a stop.

Do not promise that restriction or sealing destroys the record, prevents disqualification in the manner of a first-offender discharge under § 42-8-63.1, or supersedes disclosure required by federal law.
Do not write the participant's own statement of what has changed; the packet formats what the participant supplies and assesses none of it.
Do not hardcode a court, county, case number, OTN, judge or prosecuting attorney; every one is a case fact from the participant's own record.
Do not extend this family to the pardoned-conviction route or to the sealing-only route; each has its own track.

finalVerificationRequirements: Copy the convicting court and its level, county, case number, OTN, arrest date, adjudication date and exact O.C.G.A. Code section from the final disposition, the case papers and the Georgia criminal history report, never from memory.
Confirm every term of the sentence is complete and that four conviction-free years, in any jurisdiction excluding nonserious traffic offenses, immediately precede the filing date.
Read every numbered statement in the motion; each is pleaded as the defendant's own statement, and any that is not true is a reason not to file.
Confirm the filing method, any fee, any pauper's-affidavit practice and any standing preference on proposed orders with the clerk of the convicting court before filing; the packet quotes no figure.
Confirm the prosecuting attorney and clerk of court to be served, serve by certified mail, e-filing or hand delivery, and complete the certificate only when the copies actually go out.
The defendant signs and dates the motion and certificate as Defendant, Pro Se where unrepresented; the judge's name, SO ORDERED date and signature block are never pre-filled.

sections.heading: The defendant, Jordan Avery Reyes, files this motion in the above-styl
sections.body:
The defendant, {{participant_full_legal_name}}, files this motion in the above-styled criminal case, in the existing case under the existing case number, under O.C.G.A. § 35-3-37(j)(4)(A) and § 35-3-37(m). The defendant states:

1. The defendant was convicted of a misdemeanor offense, or of a series of misdemeanor offenses arising from a single incident, in the above-styled case.

2. The defendant has completed the terms of the sentence, including any probation, fines and restitution.

3. The defendant has not been convicted of any crime in any jurisdiction, excluding nonserious traffic offenses, for at least four years immediately preceding the filing of this motion.

4. The defendant has no pending charged offenses in any jurisdiction.

5. The offense of conviction is not an offense excluded by O.C.G.A. Sec. 35-3-37(j)(4)(B), and the lifetime maximum of two restrictions under O.C.G.A. Sec. 35-3-37(j)(4)(C) has not been reached. The exclusions turn on the exact Code section of conviction, which the defendant states below.

6. The harm otherwise resulting to the defendant clearly outweighs the public interest in the criminal history record information being publicly available.

PROPOSED ORDER RESTRICTING ACCESS TO CRIMINAL HISTORY RECORD INFORMATION AND SEALING THE RECORD OF THE CASE
(O.C.G.A. § 35-3-37(j)(4)(A) and § 35-3-37(m))

sections.heading: (This page is proposed by the defendant for the Court's consideration,
sections.body:
(This page is proposed by the defendant for the Court's consideration, as the controlling practice directs a proposed order always accompany the filing. Every order line below is completed, signed and dated only by the Court.)

Before the Court is the Defendant's Motion to Restrict and Seal Records of a Misdemeanor Conviction under O.C.G.A. Sec. 35-3-37(j)(4)(A) and Sec. 35-3-37(m).

IT IS ORDERED that the Georgia Crime Information Center (GCIC) and every agency in the county named in the caption, including the arresting agency and the jail or detention center, restrict all criminal history record information pertaining to this case, identified by the OTN and the date of arrest stated below, pursuant to O.C.G.A. Sec. 35-3-37(j)(4)(A).

IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that the Clerk of the court named in the caption seal the record of this case, including index references and online records, pursuant to O.C.G.A. Sec. 35-3-37(m).

Disclosure of the restricted and sealed information remains limited to what O.C.G.A. Sec. 35-3-37(t) and (v) permit.

filingDestination.statement: File with the clerk of the convicting court in the existing criminal case, under the existing case number, styled State of Georgia v. Defendant, by e-filing where the court accepts it. Confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing: no statewide judiciary form exists, local courts control their own filing and e-filing practice, some clerks resist accepting motions in closed criminal cases, and some judges have standing preferences on proposed orders.
filingDestination.sourceOfRule: GA.memo.json track ga-misd-j4, geography.venue, destination and rules.filing

feeAndWaiver.statement: No statutory filing fee is identified. Because the relief is a motion in an existing criminal case rather than a new civil action, the leading Georgia pro se practice does not budget one; whether any Georgia clerk charges a fee for such a filing is unresolved and county-specific, so no figure is quoted and the participant asks the clerk of the convicting court before filing.
feeAndWaiver.waiverStatement: Unresolved: the pauper's affidavit route under O.C.G.A. § 9-15-2 is designed for civil actions and its application to a filing in a criminal case is not established; the participant asks the same clerk.
feeAndWaiver.sourceOfRule: GA.memo.json track ga-misd-j4, rules.fees, rules.feeWaiver and the unresolved fee question

serviceAndNotice.statement: Notice to the prosecuting attorney, identified as District Attorney or Solicitor-General for the county; Georgia Justice Project practice also serves the clerk of court. Serve by certified mail, e-filing or hand delivery, certified in the certificate of service. No response or objection period is specified by statute.
serviceAndNotice.sourceOfRule: GA.memo.json track ga-misd-j4, rules.notice and rules.service

copyRequirements.statement: No statewide Georgia judiciary form exists for this filing and the approved legal-design record states no copy count.
copyRequirements.originalPlusCopies: Confirm the filing method, e-filing availability, copy count and any standing preference on proposed orders with the clerk of the convicting court before filing.
copyRequirements.sourceOfRule: GA.memo.json track ga-misd-j4, localFormOverride and rules.filing

postFilingTimeline.step: File the motion, proposed order, certificate and exhibits with the clerk of the convicting court in the existing criminal case, and serve the prosecuting attorney and the clerk of court.
postFilingTimeline.timing: after every term of the sentence is complete and four conviction-free years immediately precede the filing; a petition denied on the same conviction may not be refiled within two years of the final order

postFilingTimeline.step: Where a hearing is requested, the court holds it within 90 days of filing; the prosecuting attorney may oppose.
postFilingTimeline.timing: within 90 days of filing where a hearing is requested

postFilingTimeline.step: The court decides whether the harm to the individual clearly outweighs the public's interest and, if so, enters the order directing GCIC and the county agencies to restrict, and sealing the record of the case under subsection (m).
postFilingTimeline.timing: after any hearing; the finding is the court's

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The prosecuting attorney opposes the filing, or the court sets a contested hearing or takes evidence on disputed facts.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: The matter has crossed the approved self-help boundary.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: Any immigration consequence is in play.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: Immigration consequences are outside the approved self-help boundary.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The participant wants to attack the underlying conviction or charge itself.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: This route restricts and seals a record; it does not challenge the conviction.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: Venue is unclear because the trial court no longer exists or the records cannot be located.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: The convicting court retains jurisdiction for this purpose and the packet cannot choose another.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The offense classification under the § 35-3-37(j)(4)(B) exclusion list is disputed.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: The exclusions turn on the exact Code section and the packet does not decide them.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The participant has an out-of-state conviction inside the four-year window, may already have used both lifetime restriction slots, or has pending charges.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: Each is a statutory bar the packet does not resolve.

attachments.title: Copy of the final disposition
attachments.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that handled the case
attachments.whyNeeded: It supplies the adjudication date, the exact Code section and the sentence terms, and is attached as Exhibit A.

attachments.title: Your own Georgia criminal history report
attachments.conditionDescription: Where the participant relies on it or the court expects it.
attachments.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC
attachments.whyNeeded: It supplies the OTN and the arrest date and supports the four-year statement; attached as Exhibit B.

attachments.title: Proof of sentence completion, such as a probation termination order
attachments.conditionDescription: Where the participant has it or the court expects it.
attachments.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the convicting court, or the supervising probation office
attachments.whyNeeded: Sentence completion is a separate statutory requirement; attached as Exhibit C.

attachments.title: Participant-supplied supporting exhibits
attachments.conditionDescription: Where the participant chooses to supply them.
attachments.whyNeeded: Diplomas, certificates, letters of support, treatment records or evidence of community involvement support the harm-outweighs showing; attached as Exhibit D and assessed by nobody.

participantChecklist.text: Gather the final disposition and, where relied on, the Georgia criminal history report and proof of sentence completion, and fill every dotted blank from them.
Read every numbered statement in the motion; each is pleaded as your own, and if any is not true of your case do not file.
Confirm the filing method, any fee, any pauper's-affidavit practice and any proposed-order preference with the clerk of the convicting court before filing.
Sign and date the motion yourself, as Defendant, Pro Se where unrepresented; no notarization is required or added.
Serve the prosecuting attorney and the clerk of court by certified mail, e-filing or hand delivery, and complete the certificate only when the copies actually go out.
